issue: Panel A states 'on-node only (NVLink)' as an absolute property of tensor-parallel all-reduce, but TP can span nodes over fabric; the caption's 'canonical configuration' qualifier is not carried into the panel label.
evidence: Panel A text: 'communication: all-reduce every layer → on-node only (NVLink)'. Caption: 'The panels show the canonical configuration ... substitute the actual collective and schedule for the target stack.' The panel text lacks 'canonical' or 'typically'.
acceptance_test: Add a scope qualifier in the panel ('canonical: on-node/NVLink; multi-node TP possible over fabric at higher cost') or move the qualifier into the panel label so the claim is not read as universal.

issue: Panel C states 'throughput scales linearly' for data-parallel inference without the shared-bottleneck qualification; this is an idealized claim, not a general property.
evidence: Panel C text: 'inference: independent replicas, no sync · throughput scales linearly'. Caption labels the figure '[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]' but the panel text is unqualified.
acceptance_test: Qualify the claim: 'idealized: near-linear until a shared bottleneck (network, load balancer, power, storage) binds' or move 'scales linearly' into the caption with an explicit assumption.

issue: The caption claims each panel names what splits, what is replicated, and what communicates, but Panel A does not label replicated activations and Panel B does not label replicated state (or state that no model replication occurs).
evidence: Caption: 'Each panel names what splits, what is replicated, and what communicates.' Panel A shows only W0/W1, GPU 0/1, and all-reduce; Panel B shows layer ranges, P2P, and bubble; neither contains a 'replicated' label. Only Panel C labels 'full model (replica)'.
acceptance_test: Either add the missing replication labels to Panels A and B, or revise the caption to say the panels name what splits and what communicates, with replication called out only where relevant.

issue: The 'idle (bubble) at fill/drain' annotation is placed under GPU 0 only, which can imply the pipeline bubble is local to the first stage rather than a pipeline-wide fill/drain effect.
evidence: Panel B: the label sits beneath the GPU 0 box; the caption describes 'an idle bubble at fill/drain' generally.
acceptance_test: Move the label to a bracket spanning all stages or add 'pipeline-wide' to the label.

issue: The legend assigns orange to 'GPU', but the weight-to-GPU arrows in Panel A are also orange, creating a gratuitous color-semantics conflict.
evidence: Legend: 'GPU (orange)'. Panel A: arrows from W0/W1 to GPU 0/1 are orange. The arrows represent weight distribution, not GPUs.
acceptance_test: Use neutral/black arrows for data flow, or add 'arrows = data flow' to the legend and reserve orange for GPU boxes.

issue: The caption misdescribes the diagram's axes: it says 'each row is one decode step' and that 'step boundaries are staggered across rows', but each row is a slot/sequence over time and decode steps are synchronized across rows.
evidence: Caption: 'The horizontal axis is time (decode steps / iterations); each row is one decode step, and in the continuous panel the step boundaries are staggered across rows...' The figure shows four rows (slots) with multiple blue/green segments along the horizontal time axis; the rows are not individual decode steps.
acceptance_test: Rewrite the caption to: 'The horizontal axis is decode steps; each row is one slot/sequence. Decode steps are synchronized across rows; sequence start/finish times are staggered as requests are admitted and evicted.' Add a vertical step grid if needed.

issue: The discrete-batching panel does not show short outputs finishing early: all four blue sequence segments have the same length and the pink idle region begins at the same x-position in every row, so the claimed 'short outputs idle in the trailing slots' is not illustrated.
evidence: Caption: 'a batch is locked until its slowest member finishes, so short outputs idle in the trailing slots.' In the discrete panel, all four blue segments are equal width; no row has a shorter blue segment followed by idle while another row continues. The 'next batch waits' arrow points only at the bottom row.
acceptance_test: Redraw the discrete panel with staggered sequence lengths (e.g., row 1 short, row 2 medium, row 3 long, row 4 longest); show idle only in rows whose sequence has finished while longer rows continue; start the next batch after the longest row completes.

issue: The title and caption claim the four concerns are 'orthogonal' and 'independent dials' that can be combined 'any mechanism with any other', but the concerns interact in practice (e.g., continuous batching depends on KV memory management; prefix caching affects scheduling and memory; P/D disaggregation changes resource pools).
evidence: Figure title: 'Serving = four orthogonal concerns, not a stack'. Caption: 'The four are independent dials — a system can combine any mechanism with any other'. The figure shows four isolated boxes with no interaction arrows.
acceptance_test: Soften to 'separable concerns' and add a note that they are conceptually distinct but operationally coupled; or show the key interactions (scheduling↔state management, reuse↔state management, specialization↔scheduling).

issue: The figure label uses British 'SPECIALISATION' while the book elsewhere uses 'specialization' (e.g., page 185 caption 'specialization benefit'), creating terminology/spelling drift.
evidence: Figure 11.2 box: 'RESOURCE SPECIALISATION'. Page 185 caption: 'specialization benefit'. Page 184 caption also uses 'specialisation'.
acceptance_test: Choose one spelling and apply it consistently across figure labels, captions, and body text.

issue: The subtitle says 'the split is the same', but Panel A uses 4 prefill + 4 decode GPUs in one 8×H100 host while Panel B uses 8 prefill + 8 decode GPUs across two 8×H100 hosts; the resource split is not the same, which confounds the visual comparison of link cost.
evidence: Subtitle: 'the split is the same; the transfer link — and its cost — is not'. Panel A: '8× H100 host' containing 4 prefill GPUs and 4 decode GPUs. Panel B: separate '8× H100 host' for prefill and '8× H100 host' for decode, i.e., 8+8 GPUs.
acceptance_test: Hold the pool size constant across panels (e.g., 4+4 in both) or explicitly label the different pool sizes and state that the comparison isolates link bandwidth, not total capacity.

issue: The panel labels use 'PRE-FILL' while the caption and body use 'prefill', creating a hyphenation/terminology inconsistency.
evidence: Panel A and B labels: 'PRE-FILL'. Caption: 'prefill/decode partitions'. Body text: 'prefill'.
acceptance_test: Use 'PREFILL' or 'prefill' consistently in figure labels and prose.

issue: The caption says dashed arrows bring 'the complete path' to the qualification gate, but the dashed arrows originate at the hardware boxes only, visually implying that only hardware is qualified rather than the full stack.
evidence: Caption: 'dashed arrows bring the complete path to the qualification gate.' Figure: dashed arrows start at the bottom of each 'Hardware' box and point to the gate; no bracket spans the serving engine, backend entry, kernels/runtime, and hardware.
acceptance_test: Redraw the dashed arrows from a bracket spanning the full column (or from the serving engine/whole stack) to the gate, and label the arrow 'complete path'.

issue: The qualification-gate box compresses its criteria into a dense line with ambiguous '|' and ';' separators, making it unclear whether items are conjuncts or alternatives; this weakens the figure's main takeaway.
evidence: Gate box text: 'Weights + KV + workspace | operators + attention/cache path; Correctness + isolation | collectives (if used) | measured SLO'. The caption expands these into a list, but the figure itself does not make the grouping clear.
acceptance_test: Replace the bars/semicolons with bullets or explicit 'and' phrasing; separate memory residency, operator coverage, correctness/isolation, collectives, and measured SLO into readable lines.

issue: The top row is labeled 'Serving engine', but the Client NPU entry is 'OpenVINO GenAI supported NPU models', which is a toolkit/pipeline rather than a serving engine; this blurs the engine-versus-stack distinction.
evidence: Figure: 'Serving engine' box for Client NPU contains 'OpenVINO GenAI supported NPU models'. Page 188 text refers to 'OpenVINO GenAI documentation ... LLMPipeline and VLMPipeline'.
acceptance_test: Relabel the row 'Serving stack/engine' or change the Client NPU entry to 'OpenVINO GenAI LLMPipeline/VLMPipeline'.
